links.outcome: Radiologist panel preference for AI-generated versus clinician-written chest X-ray reports on the same cases
links.effect: 56.1% of ICU AI reports preferable or equivalent to clinician reports by half or more of panel; 77.7% for in/outpatient overall; 94% for cases with no pertinent abnormal findings.
links.quote: We observe a wide distribution of preferences across the panel and across clinical settings, with 56.1% of Flamingo-CXR intensive care reports evaluated to be preferable or equivalent to clinician reports, by half or more of the panel, rising to 77.7% for in/outpatient X-rays overall and to 94% for the subset of cases with no pertinent abnormal findings.

links.outcome: Clinically significant errors in AI-generated and human-written radiology reports found by expert radiologist review
links.effect: In in/outpatient cases, 24.8% had clinically significant errors in both report types, 22.8% in Flamingo-CXR reports only, 14.0% in human reports only.
links.quote: Errors were observed in human-written reports and Flamingo-CXR reports, with 24.8% of in/outpatient cases containing clinically significant errors in both report types, 22.8% in Flamingo-CXR reports only and 14.0% in human reports only.

unlisted_practices: Assistive clinician-AI collaboration setting where AI drafts are edited for reports containing errors

screen.reason: Empirical study testing clinician-AI collaboration (human-in-the-loop assistance) versus solo generation for radiology reporting using a vision-language foundation model.
